answer: Each identity registers one timber lot on an atlas, locks 80 credits, and presents it at a knoll checkpoint. The verifier matches the lot hash to the atlas entry and records one check-in per lot; a repeat presentation burns its bond. Fees rise with check-ins: the kth identity pays 18 plus 3 per earlier check-in, so the 1,000th pays 3,015 and 1,000 fakes pay 1,516,500 plus 80,000 locked bonds. A timber-rental ring fails: a rented lot has a knoll check-in, so reuse flags it for audit. An honest identity presents one lot, pays 18, and recovers its bond after a check.
